EXPLANATION
OF
BANDUNG CITY REGIONAL REGULATION
NUMBER 7 OF 2025
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals and between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.

Women have equal rights with men, however in certain discriminatory conditions, the government is obliged to implement affirmative action so that the rights of women and women in vulnerable groups need to receive protection so as not to experience violence and can live a decent life according to the principles of humanity, equality and justice. Women's empowerment and women's protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data.

The Bandung City Government as the party that has the authority to regulate and protect the citizens of Bandung City, deems it necessary to continuously carry out and formulate regulations to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and women's protection in Bandung City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various development sectors, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

CHAPTER V
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One
General

Article 15
(1) Every woman who is a victim of an act of violence has the right to obtain continuous protection and treatment up to the rehabilitation stage.
(2) The treatment of women victims of acts of violence must be kept confidential unless otherwise stipulated by the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain professional assistance services based on the victim’s condition and needs.
(4) The Regional Government provides integrated services for comprehensive and integrated protection and treatment.
(5) Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Women’s Empowerment and child protection affairs.

Article 16
(1) Forms of Violence against Women include:
   a. physical violence;
   b. sexual violence;
   c. economic violence; and
   d. psychological violence.
(2) Forms of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a include any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forcing a person to have intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or other non-commercial purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c include neglect of Women by not providing proper living support.
(5) Forms of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to the victim.

Article 17
(1) Every Woman victim of acts of violence must receive protection in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Protection of Women victims of acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided to Women who experience acts of violence in the family environment, the community, the education environment, offices, and the business world.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City Region hereinafter referred to as Region is the City Region of Bandung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bandung.
4. Regional Administration is the implementation of government affairs by the regional government and regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy in the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a Regional People's Representative Institution which is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Woman is a person or human being who has a womb, experiences menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding.
7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
8. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention.
9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward and downward up to the third degree.
10. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether legal entity or non-legal entity.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women.
13. Service is activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Handling is actions taken to provide complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement, legal services, repatriation, and social reintegration.
15. Companion is a person who is trusted and has the competence to accompany Victims in accessing the right to handling, protection and recovery.
16. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions during the service process.
17. Institution is an Office/Agency/Bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Children Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a technical operational implementation unit in a work unit that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of Integrated Services for women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
20. Integrated Service is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for Victims, Victims' Families, and/or Witnesses of Sexual Violence Crimes.

DECIDES:
To Establish REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN.

EXPLANATION
OF
BANDUNG CITY REGIONAL REGULATION
NUMBER 7 OF 2025
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals and between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.

Women have equal rights with men, however in certain discriminatory conditions, the government is obliged to implement affirmative action so that the rights of women and women in vulnerable groups need to receive protection so as not to experience violence and can live a decent life according to the principles of humanity, equality and justice. Women's empowerment and women's protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data.

The Bandung City Government as the party that has the authority to regulate and protect the citizens of Bandung City, deems it necessary to continuously carry out and formulate regulations to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and women's protection in Bandung City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various development sectors, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

6.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text includes explicit protections/services for victims/witnesses in the legal process. Pasal 20 ayat (3) defines "Pelindungan hukum" as services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes by providing legal aid, legal consultation, and legal accompaniment. Pasal 21 further lists measures for witnesses/victims including rapid handling (huruf a), confidentiality (huruf c), and guaranteeing justice/legal certainty (huruf d). The retrieved English passage [6.8-21] contains this information, and the judge’s rationale is supported by the Indonesian text. Thus the golden label "No" appears wrong; it should be "Yes".
